facts.businessType: Residential landscape design and build studio
facts.businessDescription: Cedar & Stone Landscapes is a design-build studio for residential gardens and outdoor rooms. The studio handles the full arc: site walkthrough, planting and hardscape design, sourcing, construction and first-season care. Work ranges from small city gardens to full backyard transformations with terraces, fire areas and shade structures.
facts.idealClientProfile: Homeowners planning a full garden or backyard renovation, typically moving into or remodeling a detached house. Decision maker: the homeowner or couple managing the project directly. Website purpose: book a design consultation walk-through.
extraInformation: Positioning: grounded, craft-led, patient, botanical. Supporting message: gardens designed to mature well, built by the same hands that drew them.

Services (exactly these four): Garden Design — site analysis, planting plans and hardscape drawings for the whole plot. Build & Construction — terraces, paths, retaining walls, raised beds and shade structures built by the studio's own crew. Planting & Care — sourcing, installation and a first-season care program for establishing planting. Outdoor Rooms — fire areas, covered seating and dining spaces treated as extensions of the house.

Process, four stages: 01 Walk the site — sun, soil, drainage and how you actually want to live outside. 02 Design — planting and hardscape plans, materials and a phased budget. 03 Build — the studio's own crew constructs the hardscape and planting. 04 First season — establishment care and adjustment visits through the first growing season.
Things to emphasize: hand-built stonework, four-season planting interest, working with Portland's rain and shade, small crews who stay on one project start to finish.
Strict content constraints: do not invent testimonials, client names, awards, certifications, years in business, team bios, pricing or any statistics. Never fabricate before/after claims.

creativeDirection.direction: Northwest craft almanac: a warm, botanical field-guide feel — deep forest greens against warm cedar and paper tones, oversized serif display type, generous hand-set-looking margins, and close-crop garden photography that bleeds off the container edge like pressed specimens
creativeDirection.audience: Homeowners 35-60 investing in a long-horizon garden renovation; values craft and patience over speed
creativeDirection.serviceEnvironment: Residential gardens in a rainy, green Pacific Northwest city; muddy boots, real weather, mature plants
creativeDirection.preferredPalette: Deep forest green #24382B, warm cedar #A9683C, paper cream #F4EFE4, charcoal ink #23211C, moss accent #7A8450
creativeDirection.visualStyle: Editorial field-guide: asymmetric layouts, numbered chapters, botanical close-ups at unusual crops, generous margins, hairline rules like an almanac
creativeDirection.tone: Grounded, patient, craftsmanlike; quietly confident, never salesy
creativeDirection.avoidances: No generic three-card service grids, no stock lawns or sprinkler stock photos, no purple gradients, no rounded SaaS cards
creativeDirection.inspirationNotes: Old botanical almanacs, seed catalogues with numbered plates, Japanese garden pruners on cedar benches
